questions.question: Hazardous material containers must be:

options.text: Secured so they don't move during transport.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured so they don't move during transport.
questions.explanation: Hazardous material containers must be secured. They should not fall, slide, or bounce around while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: The identification number for a hazardous material should appear:
questions.explanation: The ID number must appear on the material's shipping papers and packaging. It must also appear on cargo tanks and other bulk containers.

questions.question: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must have fire extinguishers with a minimum rating of:
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must have a fire extinguisher rated 10 B:C or higher.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a list to check for hazardous materials?

options.text: The List of Hazardous Substances and Reportable Quantities

questions.explanation: There are three main lists for identifying hazardous materials: the Hazardous Materials Table, the List of Hazardous Substances and Reportable Quantities, and the List of Marine Pollutants. The Periodic Table of Elements is not used for this purpose.

questions.question: If a package contains liquid containers, it must display:

options.text: Arrows showing the correct upright direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows showing the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Packages with liquids must have orientation arrows. These arrows show which way the package should be positioned.

questions.question: A sign that cargo contains hazardous materials is:

options.text: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
The cargo comes from a supermarket.
The cargo is in cardboard boxes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums are often used to store and transport hazardous materials. The type of container can indicate whether the cargo is hazardous.

questions.question: When transporting explosives, you may leave your vehicle unattended:
questions.explanation: You may only leave your vehicle unattended in a safe haven. A safe haven is an approved location for parking unattended vehicles loaded with explosives.

questions.question: Shippers must keep a copy of shipping papers for at least:
questions.explanation: Shippers must keep shipping papers for hazardous materials for at least two years from when the material is picked up. For hazardous waste, the time period is three years.

questions.question: When transporting large quantities of explosives:

options.text: The vehicle must always be placarded.
The vehicle must be placarded only if carrying more than 200 pounds.
The vehicle does not need to be placarded.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle must always be placarded.
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying explosives must be placarded no matter the amount. Attach placards before driving.

questions.question: Where can you find the identification numbers for chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook (ERG)

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook (ERG)
questions.explanation: The four-digit identification numbers for hazardous chemicals are listed in the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook (ERG).

questions.question: To choose the right placard, you need to know:

options.text: The hazard class of the materials.
The type of container holding the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard class of the materials.
questions.explanation: You must know the hazard class of the materials being shipped. You also need to know how much hazardous material is being shipped and the total weight of all hazardous materials in your vehicle.

questions.question: A placard should be placed:

options.text: At least three inches away from any other markings.
Under a ladder if space is limited.
On a background that matches the placard color.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least three inches away from any other markings.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed at least three inches away from other markings. Keep the placard clear of doors, ladders, and other attachments. Always place placards against a background with a different color.

questions.question: A shipment may contain hazardous materials if:

options.text: The shipper deals in fireworks or munitions.
Your last shipment was labeled hazardous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper deals in fireworks or munitions.
questions.explanation: One sign of hazardous materials is the shipper's business type. Examples include paint dealers, chemical suppliers, scientific supply houses, pest control businesses, farm supply firms, and explosives or fireworks dealers.

questions.question: Shippers package hazardous materials to ____ them.
questions.explanation: Shippers package hazardous materials to completely contain them. Vehicles must display placards to warn others about the cargo.

questions.question: If a driver gets a leaking package, they should:

options.text: Leave it on the side of the road.

questions.explanation: Drivers must refuse to take any leaking packages or shipments of hazardous materials.

questions.question: You may leave a vehicle carrying explosives unattended in:

options.text: On the shoulder of a highway.

questions.explanation: You may only leave a vehicle with explosives unattended at a safe haven. A safe haven is an approved location for parking unattended vehicles loaded with explosives.

questions.question: If you find leaking cargo, you should:

options.text: Touch it to identify what it is.
Use shipping papers and labels to identify it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify it.
questions.explanation: Use shipping papers, labels, or package location to identify leaking hazardous materials. Never touch the leaking material.

questions.question: If your vehicle with explosives breaks down, warn other drivers with:

options.text: Standing on the road and waving your arms.

questions.explanation: Use reflective triangles or red electric lights for warning signals. Never use flares or other burning signals when transporting explosives.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, park at least ____ from any building.
questions.explanation: Do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, building, gathering place, or open fire when carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives.

questions.question: When a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, hazardous materials may need to be:

options.text: Circled with a pen or marker.

questions.explanation: Mark hazardous materials on shipping papers in one of three ways: list them first, highlight them in a different color, or mark them with an "X" in the "HM" column.
